meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, and I'd like to know who decided on the zero before anyone spoke to Owen.
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
I'm writing that down: 612 words, 11:52 PM. What date was that, and where is the page?
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.
"Maybe." This isn't about making me happy, Hale. Is the zero withdrawn or isn't it, and will you put in writing that nothing goes on his record?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen found out, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position; nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record, with the principal next if she doesn't get it.
What moved her: Nothing; the version history had a time and a word count but no date and no page she could check, so it didn't count as evidence yet.
What cost ground: Offering to drop the zero as a favour to make her happy, because it sounded like a hedge and a bargain, not a correction, and she never got a clear answer.
Try next time: When she asked what date the 612 words arrived, answer that first and show her the page, before saying anything about the zero.
